arm: cheribsd-purecap, default async revocation, quarantine disposition only
what_this_bundle_is: NOT a verdict. The verdicts for these eight cases are in results/20261006-cheribsd and they are MISSES. This bundle answers the one question a miss leaves open: was the object in CheriBSD's revocation quarantine and simply not swept yet, or did it never get there at all?
question: Cases 0-7 of memcached/allocator-repros are clean on stock CheriBSD under default revocation. Is the stale object quarantined but unswept, or never in the quarantine?
answer: never in the quarantine. cache.c and the slab layer recycle the object on memcached's own freelists; it never reaches free()
how_measured: ports/common/host/cheribsd/quarantine-probe.c, sha256 fa283f7686c36e1803910e006dc429577ee132fd6eea12ef49a89b6b97263554, LD_PRELOADed in front of the case through the shared runner's per-case env. It wraps malloc, calloc, realloc and free and reads the kernel's revocation shadow bitmap, one bit per 16-byte granule, set while that granule is quarantined, plus the dequeue epoch whose advance counts completed sweeps. Nothing forces a sweep. Measured twice: once with a version that wrapped only malloc and free, then again with this one, and every counter is identical -- the port calls no realloc on this path.
numbers: quarantine.tsv, one row per case: the probe's four counters beside the program's own reuse counters from its MCP report
why_that_settles_it: not the zero in reused_while_quarantined on its own. sweeps=0 in every case, so nothing freed was ever cleared and a stale read would have succeeded without any reissue; that column cannot distinguish the two silences here. What settles it is the SIZE of the frees column: four to six libc frees in the whole process, all of them quarantined, which is process infrastructure -- with four frees in total the item cannot have passed through free(). Meanwhile the program's own counters show the reuse that carries each defect one layer down: object_reuses on cases 0 and 1, chunk_reuses on 2-4, chunk_releases on 5-7. The object does not cross the system allocator's boundary, so revocation never sees it. The silence is structural.

controls.the_probe_does_not_disable_revocation: revocation-control ran first with the probe loaded and still faulted at its labelled load: signal=34 code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) addr=pc=0x101e42, after printing revocation=1 tag_after_sweep=0 reissued=1
controls.the_platform_controls_passed: cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds, the shared runner's own, both PASS
controls.case_8_still_faults_with_the_probe_loade: the one case this arm catches faults with the probe in place, but with code=1 (PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS), not code=2: it is a SPATIAL catch from per-object bounds, not a temporal one. Recorded because an oracle written for a tag fault rejects it, and the rejection is the oracle's error, not the platform's
controls.the_sweep_counter_is_live: measured on the same probe in the same boot through mruby: 400,811 allocations churned reports sweeps=22, a quiet run reports 0. Without that pair a zero here would be indistinguishable from a dead counter. See ../../../../mruby/release-differential/results/20261008-cheribsd-quarantine.

every_free_was_not_used: _RUNTIME_REVOCATION_EVERY_FREE_ENABLE=1 is not a substitute and was not run here. On perl it made all eleven cases fault, including one that is an in-bounds read of a live object which no mechanism may legitimately catch, so that configuration cannot tell a catch from an artefact
generality: the same finding, measured the same way, settles perl/release-differential case 5 -- see its results/20261006-cheribsd, is_the_extra_case_in_the_quarantine. Two programs, two nested allocators, one answer
contrast: mruby's four temporal system-allocator cases, measured the same day with the same probe, come out the OTHER way: quarantined-unswept. mruby frees straight through libc, nineteen hundred frees a case, so its stale block does enter the quarantine and the async window is what loses it. A CheriBSD miss is not one phenomenon.
